note: disposition: bound (confirmed against the implementation) | approximated (maps with stated loss) | unsupported (declared, with stated behaviour) | unverified (coverage detected, mapping not yet confirmed by a human). Only bound rows are claims; unverified rows are work.

visible.notes: Sets `node.visible` from a boolean. A `$binding` value is skipped by an earlier guard, and the conditional form is deferred to the paired-visibility feature — both are declared at the value-form level.

opacity.notes: A TokenReference binds the variable; otherwise the raw number is written.

locked.notes: Canvas interaction only — the Plugin API can still mutate a locked node, so it applies wherever it is reached, children included.

backgroundColor.notes: Reads Figma's `fills`; the name diverges because a spec names the role the colour plays, not the Figma property it came from (ADR-009). Resolves in four steps — gradient, resolved style, bound variable, cached raw value — and writes a single solid paint. A token with neither a resolvable variable nor a cached raw value is skipped with a warning, which is the degradation DSPEC-43 permits. Loss: `colorSpace` is never read, so components are taken as sRGB regardless; a `none` component becomes 0; components beyond the third are dropped. Never applied to a text node.

backgroundImage.notes: Appends an image paint rather than replacing existing fills. Loss: `objectFit` is binary — `CONTAIN` becomes Figma's FIT and everything else, including absent, becomes FILL. An image whose hash does not resolve is dropped with no warning. Container types only.

fillColor.notes: Reads Figma's `fills`; the name diverges because a spec names the role the colour plays (ADR-013). A gradient takes its own path; otherwise the same four-step paint resolution. On an instance the target is the first fillable descendant, found by walking the subtree. Loss: the colour-space issue above, and an instance with no fillable descendant drops the value silently.

textColor.notes: Reads Figma's `fills`; the name diverges because a spec names the role the colour plays (ADR-009). Text nodes only, using the same four-step paint resolution. Loss: the colour-space issue above.

clipsContent.notes: Container types only; the key never reaches another type because no other key list admits it.

cornerRadius.notes: A uniform value sets the node radius; a token also binds the variable to all four corner fields; a per-corner object expands to Figma's physical corner properties. Not applied to a text node.

minWidth.notes: Loss: a value of 0 is written as `null`, because the Plugin API rejects zero for a minimum. An explicit zero minimum and an absent one are therefore indistinguishable on the canvas. Skipped on text nodes.

minHeight.notes: Same zero-to-null remap as `minWidth`, for the same API reason.

maxWidth.notes: Written as resolved. Zero is preserved, because a maximum of zero is a real if unusual constraint and the API accepts it. Skipped on text nodes.

maxHeight.notes: Written as resolved, preserving zero, as `maxWidth`.

strokes.notes: The same four-step paint resolution, written to the node's strokes. Loss: the colour-space issue above. Never applied to a text node, and absent from an instance's key list.

strokeAlign.notes: Passed through unchanged. The schema types this as an open string rather than an enum, so there is no mapping to lose. A `null` is skipped rather than resetting the node's current alignment.

strokeWeight.notes: A number sets the weight; a token also binds the variable to all four per-side fields; a per-side object expands to Figma's physical stroke-weight properties.

strokeDashPattern.notes: The schema's `{ dash, gap }` becomes Figma's two-element dash array, which is exactly what the property takes. The schema permits no longer pattern — both members are required and no others are allowed — so nothing is truncated.

typography.notes: Accepts Typography or TokenReference. A font that fails to load degrades to Inter Regular with a warning, never aborts.

textAlignHorizontal.notes: Inverts the capture mapping: the schema's logical `START`, `CENTER`, `END` and `JUSTIFY` become Figma's physical `LEFT`, `CENTER`, `RIGHT` and `JUSTIFIED`. All four schema values are covered, so the fallback is unreachable for valid input. Requires the node's font to be loaded first.

textAlignVertical.notes: Passed through unchanged. The schema types this as an open string, and Figma's own values match, so the identity mapping loses nothing. Text nodes only.

textOverflow.notes: Remaps the schema's two values to Figma's truncation vocabulary: `ELLIPSIS` becomes ENDING and `CLIP` becomes DISABLED. Both schema values are covered. Ordering matters — `maxLines` is honoured only while truncation is ENDING, so it is deliberately applied after this key.

maxLines.notes: Deferred to last — honoured only while textTruncation is ENDING, so textOverflow must land first.

mainAxisAlignment.notes: Remaps all four schema values to Figma's primary-axis vocabulary. Gated on the node actually having the property, which effectively means an auto-layout container.

primaryAxisSizingMode.notes: Deferred after layoutSizingHorizontal/Vertical, which themselves write it — the shorthand would otherwise clobber the explicit primitive.

crossAxisAlignment.notes: Remaps `START`, `END`, `CENTER` and `BASELINE`. Loss: `STRETCH` is a schema value Figma's counter-axis property cannot express, and it is skipped with a warning — a declared degradation that applies nothing and says so, which is exactly what DSPEC-43 asks for.

itemReverseZIndex.notes: Auto-layout only — a frame with no layoutMode has nothing to reverse. layoutMode is structural and applied first.

padding.notes: A uniform value or token sets all four sides; a per-side object expands to Figma's physical padding properties. Loss: `start` always becomes the left padding and `end` the right, with no writing-direction branch, so a right-to-left context renders mirrored. A side omitted from the object is left at its current value rather than reset.

aspectRatio.notes: Deferred to last — the lock reads the node final dimensions, so an earlier resize would be clobbered by later sizing keys.

autoVsAbsoluteLayout.notes: Per axis. These keys are computed from constraints and geometry, never read from a single Figma property — a binding presenting them as direct reads misleads anyone implementing a second time. ADR-041 governs the constraint mapping.

cases.why: a root has no parent bounds to be positioned within, and where a designer dragged it on the canvas is not part of its spec
a flow-placed child's position comes from the parent's stack, so recording offsets would assert a placement it does not have

emit: offsets per the per-axis table below
`position` ABSOLUTE when `node.layoutPositioning` is ABSOLUTE or any offset was set, otherwise null
cases.why: an element placed by coordinates rather than a parent's stack is absolutely positioned whatever Figma reports, because a regular frame has no stack to opt out of

emit: the leading edge offset — `start` or `top` — set to the node position
the trailing edge offset — `end` or `bottom` — set to parent dimension less node position less node dimension
the matching centre offset, set to node position plus half the node dimension less half the parent dimension
both edge offsets on the axis
axisCases.why: a stretched node is defined by its edges, not its size

emit: both edge offsets on the axis, as percentage strings

relationCases.why: a hugged or filled axis has no fixed dimension to record
an absolutely positioned child is not sized by the parent axis

otherwise.why: a flow-placed child in auto-layout records no positioning offsets

wrapping.notes: A property that cannot apply is removed rather than recorded as null, so a reader never sees a dead key.

cases.why: none of them mean anything without auto-layout. `wrapAlignment` is removed rather than nulled: the removal below also holds here, because a node with no auto-layout has no wrap either, and a first-match table that said null would describe a state no document reaches
a dead property otherwise — removed, not nulled

emit: `itemSpacing` as a biaxial composite, mapping the Figma primary and counter axes onto absolute horizontal and vertical

namedStyleVersusInline.notes: A named text style and inline typography are mutually exclusive in a document: one is a reference, the other is the resolved values. Typography sub-fields are additionally compared against their own defaults, a second and distinct default source from the style keys.

inputs.from: whether a text-style entry was captured at all, which is not the same as its value
Figma node — an empty string counts as no style, the same as null
the unvaried baseline for this element

cases.why: no text-style entry was captured for this node at all, so the pass has nothing to choose between and leaves `typography` as it found it. Distinct from an entry captured with an empty value, below
the named style is the source; resolved values beside it would be a second copy
a variant diff dropped it, but with no named style the values are the only record

boolean.notes: A native BOOLEAN property reads directly. A VARIANT whose options are exactly true/false (case-insensitive) also reads as a boolean, recording `$extensions['com.figma'].type: VARIANT` so the render direction rebuilds the variant axis rather than a BOOLEAN property. Render creates a BOOLEAN property where the prop is bound to an element's `visible`.

string.notes: TEXT and INSTANCE_SWAP both collapse to `string`; the Figma property type survives in `$extensions['com.figma'].type`. An INSTANCE_SWAP default resolves the component id to a name, reduced to the glyph name where the glyphs convention identifies one (ADR-103). The read default lands in `examples`, never `default` (ADR-014). Render re-derives the property type from where the prop is bound: `content` → TEXT, `instanceOf` → INSTANCE_SWAP.

enum.target: VARIANT property options / ComponentSet variant axes
enum.notes: The option list is the variant axis, authored order preserved — the render direction rebuilds the component set from it positionally. `nullable: false` is recorded: the enum lists every accepted value.

number.target: TEXT default or all-numeric VARIANT options, under `platforms.figma.inferNumberProps`
number.notes: Opt-in inference (ADR-029). A TEXT property whose default passes the numeric guard becomes a NumberProp; a VARIANT whose every option is numeric becomes a NumberProp carrying the options as `enum` (ADR-072). With the convention off, both stay strings.

slot.notes: Native SLOT properties read as `type: slot`. Under `platforms.figma.slotConstraints`, `slotSettings` and resolved `preferredValues` populate `minChildren`/`maxChildren`/`anyOf` (ADR-056). A primitive marker joins `anyOf` when a variant's default content held a top-level `$text`/`$glyph` primitive and the platform reads slot primitives (ADR-102) — only ever joining an `anyOf` that already names a component. `defaultSlot` resolves once at generation from `specs.slots.default.match`, is refused when the prop is bound to anything but a container or slot element, and marks at most one prop (ADR-099). Render skips slot props — slot structure is rebuilt from the elements, not minted as a property.

image.notes: An image prop has no native Figma property type; it is read from a code-only layer (ADR-063) and carries authoring-default images in `examples` (ADR-088). Render mints the hidden layer back.

object.notes: Figma cannot author an object natively. Flat names fold into one ObjectProp before key formatting (ADR-111); each member's `$extensions['com.figma'].name` records the flat source name, so unfolding on render is reversal, not re-derivation. A name colliding with the fold outcome stays flat. Render emits one flat property per member — BOOLEAN for boolean members, TEXT otherwise; enum members are variant axes and belong to the component set.

cases.why: A two-state axis is a boolean wearing variant clothes; the extension records the source so render rebuilds the axis

emit: NumberProp with the options as `enum`, authored order, `nullable: false`
cases.why: ADR-072 — the enum is the variant axis; render rebuilds the component set from it positionally

emit: EnumProp with the options as `enum`, `nullable: false`
cases.why: The default case: a closed option list

otherwise.why: Non-VARIANT property types resolve per kind, outside this cluster

variantAxes.notes: One Figma VARIANT property resolves to one of three prop kinds, and no kind alone states the rule.

emit: NumberProp with `default` and `examples` carrying the number
cases.why: ADR-029 — opt-in, so a library whose TEXT props are genuinely text never loses them to digits

emit: StringProp with the read default in `examples`
otherwise.why: The read default is demo content, never a contract default (ADR-014)

numberInference.notes: A TEXT property is a string or a number, and only the convention plus the value decide which.

codeOnlyProps.resolution: A hidden code-only container layer's sub-layers mint props the component's native property surface cannot carry — accessibility labels, heading levels, ARIA concerns, image sources (ADR-027). Each prop records `source.kind: 'codeOnlyProp'` and its `layer`; an enum minted from a nested instance records `instanceOf`. Props named in `figma.images.sourceProps` mint ImageProps (ADR-063). Native extraction skips these names so a prop is minted exactly once. Render mints the hidden layers back from the provenance.
codeOnlyProps.partial: A code-only layer with no recognisable sub-layer shape mints nothing; native props are unaffected.
codeOnlyProps.notes: Code-only extraction spans the boolean, string, number, enum and image kinds; it is keyed under `image` because that kind exists only through it — the other kinds also read natively.

outputs: the paired content prop, made nullable; the boolean prop, consumed
booleanContentPairing.resolution: A BOOLEAN property that only ever toggles the visibility of the element a content prop fills is not a second fact — it is the content prop's nullability. Where visible- and content-bindings co-occur on one element across variants and the pairing validates, the boolean is consumed and the content prop records `nullable: true`; `null` then means what the toggle meant.
booleanContentPairing.partial: A candidate pair that fails cross-variant validation leaves both props standing as read.
booleanContentPairing.notes: The consolidation rule: two Figma properties become one spec prop. The render direction re-creates the boolean from the nullable content prop's visible-binding.

text.notes: Reads from a TEXT node; render creates one. The only type that carries typography, and the only one whose `content` is a string or a content binding.

glyph.target: INSTANCE or VECTOR reclassified by the library's glyphs convention
glyph.notes: No Figma node type is a glyph. Membership comes from the declared glyphs convention — name pattern or structural form (ADR-103) — and `content` carries the glyph name. Render swaps in the glyph component's instance by name.

vector.notes: Capture records the type, position and styles — never the path geometry, which the schema does not carry. Render therefore creates an empty vector node of the right size and styling: the shape's actual paths are lost on any round trip. The declared seam, not an accident.

container.notes: The default classification: any node type without a mapping of its own. The transforms' internal key tables speak `frame` and `component` where the contract says `container` — the component ROOT is the component, not an anatomy element, and a nested frame folds to `container`. That vocabulary mapping is declared here and nowhere else.

slot.notes: Native slot nodes. The prop side of the same fact — constraints, markers, the default slot — is the props surface's `slot` kind; the element side carries `contentStyles` keyed by the primitive markers its prop's `anyOf` names (ADR-102).

instance.notes: `instanceOf` resolves to the main component's name — the component set's where the main component sits inside one. A primitive layer in composed content may be PROMOTED to an instance by the primitives convention (ADR-074), recorded in `$extensions['com.figma']`.

line.notes: Direct node-type mapping both ways; stroke styling carries the appearance.

ellipse.notes: Direct node-type mapping both ways. Arc data (sweep, ratio) is not carried by the spec; a plain ellipse round-trips cleanly.

rectangle.notes: Direct node-type mapping both ways; size, fills and corner radii carry the appearance.

polygon.notes: The node type maps directly, but the point count is not carried by the spec — render creates the default polygon.

star.notes: The node type maps directly, but the point count and inner-radius ratio are not carried by the spec — render creates the default star.

args.compareTo: matches the glyphs convention — by name pattern, or by structural form after membership is established from the node (ADR-103)

emit: `glyph` — whatever the node type, with the glyph name as `content`
cases.why: A glyph is a convention fact, not a node-type fact; an INSTANCE and a VECTOR can both be one

args.compareTo: one of TEXT, VECTOR, LINE, STAR, POLYGON, RECTANGLE, ELLIPSE, INSTANCE

otherwise.why: FRAME, COMPONENT, and any node type without a mapping of its own — the default is structural, so a new Figma node type degrades to a container rather than failing

typeDetection.notes: One node resolves to one of eleven types, and the glyph arm means no single node type determines the answer.

outputs: one anatomy element where Figma has two layers; `$extensions['com.figma'].name` and `childRole` carry the provenance
wrapperCollapse.resolution: A container wrapping exactly one primitive collapses into a single element (ADR-058), keyed by the wrapper and typed by the primitive. The pre-collapse layer name is always recorded, and a role annotated on the collapsed child is recorded as `childRole` so render can put each annotation back on the layer that carried it (ADR-083's collapse family).
wrapperCollapse.partial: A wrapper holding more than one child, or a non-primitive, does not collapse — both layers stay elements.
wrapperCollapse.notes: Gated by the collapse-primitive-wrapper setting. This is a cross-concern rule: it rewrites anatomy, element styles and binding refs together.

outputs: an `instance` element with `promotedPrimitive`, optional `multipleMatches`, and the consumed content in `$extensions['com.figma']`
primitivePromotion.resolution: A primitive layer inside composed example content whose shape matches a `conventions.primitives` entry is promoted to an instance of the matching design system component (ADR-074) — a text layer becomes a Typography instance, a glyph a dsIcon. The promotion records itself and what it consumed, so reversal and auditing stay possible; several matching entries record `multipleMatches` with the highest-scoring one chosen.
primitivePromotion.partial: A primitive matching no entry stays a primitive element.
primitivePromotion.notes: Applies in composed/example content, not to the component's own anatomy.

valueForms.summary: Every style value may be a literal, the `mixed` sentinel, a TokenReference, a PropBinding, or a Conditional. A disposition for a key means little without saying what happens to each form (DSPEC-42).
valueForms.mixedValueNote: Nothing is applied. A mixed value records that the source layer had no single value, so there is nothing to render and a rendered guess would be invented data. The sentinel is a defect signal about the Figma file, not a value a binding realises.
valueForms.tokenReferenceNote: Recognised by its `$token` key and resolved to a Figma variable. Where the variable cannot be resolved, the value falls back to the cached raw value the document carries, which is a degradation using only data the document holds (DSPEC-43).
valueForms.propBindingNote: A dedicated binding path parses `{ $binding: "#/props/NAME" }` and wires the corresponding Figma node field to the component property.
valueForms.conditionalNote: The ADR-018 conditional form is implemented on the render path: the condition’s binding target is resolved dynamically and the then/else branch applied. This is the one platform that honours it.

directions.figma-to-spec: Capture. A Figma file becomes a document.
directions.spec-to-figma: Render. A document becomes nodes on the canvas.

onAbsentVocabulary.declaredDefault: Applies the value the schema declares for an absent key.
onAbsentVocabulary.platformInitial: Applies the platform's own initial value, which may differ from the schema's declared default.
onAbsentVocabulary.unverified: Nobody has established what this platform does when the key is absent.

onAbsentNote: What this platform does when a style key is absent from a document. The schema declares the meaning of absence once (§4.1a); this records whether the platform honours it. A row whose onAbsent is not declaredDefault is a disagreement with the contract, and each one is a decision rather than an accident.

basisVocabulary.implementation: Verified against a citable implementation. The drift guard checks it, and a change to that implementation fails the build.
basisVocabulary.intent: Asserted from the authoritative source for what the data means, which is not publicly citable. Nothing mechanical checks it; a reviewer must.

basisNote: Whether a claim is checked or asserted. Figma is bidirectional: a render claim is verified against a citable implementation, while a capture claim rests on the authoritative capture engine, which is private — so nothing mechanical can check it and a reader should know that.

colorSpace.title: A non-sRGB ColorObject renders as if it were sRGB
colorSpace.note: The schema admits 14 colour spaces and the render path never reads `colorSpace` — components 0 through 2 are taken as red, green and blue regardless, so an `oklch` value is misread rather than approximated. A `none` component becomes 0, and components beyond the third are dropped.
colorSpace.decided: Convert to sRGB at render time (#813). The schema keeps all 14 spaces; the render path gains a conversion with gamut mapping for values outside sRGB. Until that lands, a non-sRGB ColorObject renders wrong rather than degraded.

explicitZero.title: Zero is not distinguishable from unset
explicitZero.note: Both platforms currently treat a dimension of 0 as "no constraint" rather than "a constraint of zero".
explicitZero.decided: Open. Deferred — see #814, and #812 on what an absent `width`/`height` means. The two interact and should be settled together.

logicalToPhysical.title: Logical sides become physical without a direction
logicalToPhysical.note: The schema uses `start` and `end` so a document is direction-agnostic. The Figma render maps `start` to the left padding with no writing-direction branch.
logicalToPhysical.decided: Accepted as a platform limit. Figma cannot express a writing direction, so the mapping is left-to-right only and the loss is declared rather than fixed — which is what `approximated` means. CSS stays direction-safe by emitting `padding-block` and `padding-inline`.

partialOnUnresolved.title: A value is dropped rather than degraded
partialOnUnresolved.note: A gradient whose stops do not yield two resolvable colours is dropped whole. A `padding` side that is present but unresolvable is omitted while its siblings emit, whereas `cornerRadius` substitutes `0` for the same failure. DSPEC-43 says a degradation applies the spec's own recorded fallback, or applies nothing and warns — dropping part of a value silently is neither.
partialOnUnresolved.decided: Open. See #816 on the disagreement between the composite types, and #815 on the gradient path.
